exposure: hemolysis elevated liver low platelet syndrome
Fetal growth restriction status (presence or absence)
administration of steroids for fetal lung maturity
severe hypertension refractory to medical therapy
outcome: Interval from diagnosis of preeclampsia to delivery
Rates of induction and cesarean delivery
Development of severe morbidities of preeclampsia
Neonatal outcomes (neonatal intensive care unit admission, prolonged neonatal stay, and neonatal mortality)
cohort: 199 pregnant women with preeclampsia diagnosed prior to 34 weeks of gestation, singleton pregnancies, and live births, managed expectantly at the University of Cincinnati Medical Center between 2008 and 2013.
finding: Fetal growth restriction is associated with a shorter interval from the diagnosis of preeclampsia to delivery in women undergoing expectant management of preeclampsia diagnosed before 34 weeks of gestation.
